title: Aspirin
mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1 → less thromboxane A2 for the platelet's lifespan

uses.doseText: Start within 48 h of onset; trials used 160–300 mg daily early (IST 300 mg, CAST 160 mg)
notes: Not a substitute for IVT or EVT in eligible patients (COR 3: Harm, B-R)

uses.agent: IV aspirin with or within 90 min of starting IVT

notes: Antiplatelet preferred over anticoagulation (AHA 2026 and Kleindorfer 2021: COR 1, A)
Choose agent on risk profile, cost, tolerance (AHA 2026: COR 1, C-EO)
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021: COR 1, LOE A (aspirin 50–325 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, or aspirin 25 mg/ER-dipyridamole 200 mg BID)

uses.agent: Aspirin — DAPT partner for minor stroke/high-risk TIA
uses.doseText: Load 160–325 mg, then 75–100 mg daily (trial regimens; see DAPT entry, pending)
notes: With ticagrelor: aspirin maintenance 75–100 mg (ticagrelor label)
evidenceNote: AHA 2026: DAPT COR 1, LOE A (clopidogrel + aspirin, 21 days)

renalHepatic: Avoid in severe renal failure (GFR <10) or severe hepatic insufficiency (aspirin/ER-dipyridamole label, aspirin component)

timing.halfLifeText: Short plasma half-life, but platelet inhibition is irreversible and lasts the platelet lifespan (7–10 days)
holdBeforeProcedure: Usually continued for LP and most neuro procedures — follow local policy
thrombolysisRule: Prior SAPT/DAPT doesn't exclude IVT — give if otherwise eligible (AHA 2026 §4.6.1 Rec 9: COR 1, B-NR); sICH +0.9% SAPT / +1.2% DAPT absolute
Not a substitute for IVT/EVT (AHA 2026 §4.8 Rec 16: COR 3: Harm, B-R)
No IV aspirin with IVT or within 90 min after start (AHA 2026 §4.8 Rec 17: COR 3: Harm, B-R)

reversal.agent: Platelet transfusion — ICH without planned surgery
notes: NCS: against, regardless of agent, platelet-function result, volume or exam
evidenceNote: AHA ICH 2022: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R (aspirin)

reversal.doseText: 1 single-donor apheresis unit; platelet-function testing first if available
notes: Repeat only if platelet function stays abnormal (NCS)
Don't transfuse if platelet function is normal or documented resistance (NCS strong)
evidenceNote: NCS 2016: conditional, moderate quality (aspirin or ADP inhibitor)

notes: Can be combined with platelet transfusion before surgery (NCS)
evidenceNote: AHA ICH 2022: COR 2b, LOE C-LD (effectiveness uncertain)

interactions: Ibuprofen can blunt low-dose aspirin's antiplatelet effect: give ibuprofen 400 mg ≥30 min after immediate-release aspirin or ≥8 h before; enteric-coated aspirin timing not established; occasional use is low risk (FDA 2006)
pregnancy: Aspirin <100 mg daily is the first-choice antiplatelet in pregnancy; safe in lactation (Miller 2026)
institutionVaries: Rectal aspirin dose in dysphagia orders
pearls: After IVT: antiplatelets in the first 24 h might be considered only with a compelling indication (AHA 2026: COR 2b, B-NR); usual practice is 24-h imaging first
Already on aspirin at the time of stroke: raising the dose or switching agents is of unclear benefit (AHA 2026: COR 2b, B-NR)
Contraindicated with NSAID allergy or the asthma/rhinitis/nasal polyp syndrome (aspirin/ER-dipyridamole label)
